articles.title: Pentagon Official Says Ukraine War Likely To Last Through Winter, Despite Mediation Efforts
articles.summary: A top Pentagon official told NATO allies that Moscow is likely to continue its war efforts in Ukraine at least through the winter months, despite Washington's attempts to secure a cease-fire and peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
articles.body: A top Pentagon official told NATO allies that Moscow is likely to continue its war efforts in Ukraine at least through the winter months, despite Washington's attempts to secure a cease-fire and peace deal between Russia and Ukraine. US Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby, speaking to alliance members in Brussels on November 17, also faced sharp pushback from US and Ukrainian allies for remarks critical of Kyiv's recent strikes deep inside Russia. Colby was speaking at a gathering of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, an informal alliance of some 50 nations that coordinates military support for Ukraine among Western allies. It is also referred to as the Ramstein group for the US air base in Germany were talks were first held. The defense undersecretary said that “as winter sets in, it appears that Russia will continue to generate more manpower and mobilize its war economy for the long haul,” adding that all must be prepared for the conflict “to endure.” Crimea Bridge Critically Damaged As Ukraine, Russia Exchange Strikes Colby said that US President Donald Trump and “remain firmly committed to bringing this conflict to an end on terms that secure a durable peace.” Trump is expected to attend a meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen together with the Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Chinese leader Xi Jinping in which the war and various attempts to end it is expected to be discussed. Trump's peace envoys, son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, are on the same day expected to attend a meeting in Berlin with the Coalition of the Willing -- a grouping led by Germany, France, and Britain set up to support Washington’s mediation efforts and potentially form a peacekeeping mission should a cease-fire be agreed upon in Ukraine. Colby also criticized Ukraine’s recent so-called deep strikes in Russian territories that has targeted both Russian energy facilities and the warehouses of the Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries. “Our assessment is that such strikes have not been effective in driving an end to the war nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line," Colby said. "Moreover, such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure, such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate." He added, however, that “Ukraine should not be forced to fight with its hands tied behind its back,” underlining that strikes “focused on the front line and direct support to that battle area is, of course," a different matter. His comments come as Ukraine struck the strategic and symbolic Kerch Bridge, connecting mainland Russia with the illegally annexed Ukrainian Crimean Peninsula, severely disrupting Kremlin efforts to supply the occupied region. The bridge is the only direct road and rail link between Russia and the Black Sea peninsula. Kyiv has struck at targets inside Russia in response to intensified Kremlin attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities, creating fuel shortages ahead of the likely brutal winter months. Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskiy told RFE/RL on November 16 that Russia's efforts are aimed at "breaking the spirit" of its people as winter approaches. Colby's remarks critical of Ukraine's strikes deep inside Russia were rejected by US and Ukrainian allies. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius rejected Colby's blasted Ukrainian air strikes in Russia as "quite a stupid thing." "Instead of criticizing Ukraine's deep strikes, better to criticize terrorist strikes every night and every day on energy, water, and heating infrastructure in Ukraine," he told reporters, citing relentless Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian sites. British defense chief Wes Streeting echoed those remarks, saying Ukraine's strikes "helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives." Rikard Jozwiak is the Europe editor for RFE/RL in Prague, focusing on coverage of the European Union and NATO. He previously worked as RFE/RL’s Brussels correspondent, covering numerous international summits, European elections, and international court rulings. He has reported from most European capitals, as well as Central Asia.

articles.title: Kosovo's Former President Thaci Found Guilty Of Obstructing Justice In War Crimes Trial
articles.summary: The Kosovo court in The Hague has found former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) commander and later Kosovar President Hashim Thaci guilty of obstruction of justice and sentenced him to 17 months in jail.
articles.body: The Kosovo court in The Hague has found former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) commander and later Kosovar President Hashim Thaci guilty of obstruction of justice and sentenced him to 17 months in jail. The sentence is on top of the 25 years he already faces after being found guilty in a separate but related war crimes trial earlier this year. Thaci faced 11 charges, including contempt of court, obstructing officials trying to carry out their duties, and violating the secrecy of court proceedings. The prosecutor, who pushed for a six-year prison sentence, noted that Thaci had instructed four former associates who visited him in detention in The Hague to persuade witnesses to testify in his favor. In September, the special tribunal in The Hague found Thaci and three other former KLA leaders who fought Serb forces in the 1998-99 war guilty of illegal and arbitrary arrest and detention, cruel treatment, torture, and murder. The verdict and the surprising long length of the sentence sparked anger and widespread protests among many in Kosovo who regarded Thaci and his co-defendants as heroes of Kosovo's independence movement. Thaci announced he would appeal the first sentence and is expected to challenge the second ruling, as well. Commenting on the November 17 ruling, the acting chairwoman of Thaci's Democratic Party of Kosovo party, Vlora Citaku, described the verdict as "shameful" and "unacceptable." Iran dismisses report of alleged 'dirty bomb' attack on Washington
articles.summary: Iran has said CNN's claim that Tehran would attack Washington with a "dirty bomb" was an attempt to manufacture further legitimacy to continue the war. Trump has said his administration takes the claim "very seriously."
articles.body: Iran on Tuesday dismissed a CNN report that Tehran was preparing a so-called "dirty bomb plot." US President Donald Trump said his administration was taking the report "very seriously." Tehran's dismissal came after CNN reported on Tuesday that "Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, DC," citing multiple US intelligence sources. The article also reported that "US intelligence has picked up Iranian chatter claiming that it has stashed bomb-making materials inside the country" and that "many national security officials assume that pre-positioned nuclear materials have already been in the US for years," citing, again, multiple US intelligence sources. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video When asked about the story during his visit to the Philippines , Trump said that if there was such a threat, Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before." "I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," he added. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei slammed the report, calling it "a malicious campaign to manufacture propaganda." "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations," he said on X. "Step by step, they are attempting to manufacture a veneer of legitimacy for further aggression and atrocities," he said, naming CNN's reporting on the alleged "dirty bomb plot" and The New York Times without specifying any of its reporting. Baghaei also said the US and Israel hit water storage reservoirs "during the recent acts of aggression." The Iran war , started by the US and Israeli strikes on February 28, continues as negotiations to bring an end to the fighting stall. Both US and Israel have been holding off from major attacks as they held elections over the last weeks. Tehran has said it is in control the Strait of Hormuz , a key transit point for global oil and natural gas supplies, while continuing to attack ships it considers unauthorized users of the waterway. There are near-daily reports of ships hitting mines in parts of the strait Tehran says are unauthorized for transit. The US Navy, which is enforcing its own blockade of Iranian vessels, has recently escorted tankers through the strait. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Before the midterm elections, Trump said, "We may do another little Epic Fury," referring to US-Israeli strikes that started the war, though he did not provide any timeframe. Trump is expected to meet Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of an APEC leaders' summit in China on Thursday and discuss ending the ​war in Iran. Pakistan-mediated peace talks between the US and Iran on April failed to reach a conclusion. Qatar, another mediator in the war, on Tuesday called for restraint "to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts." Tit-for-Tat US-Iran Attacks Persist As Peace Deal Remains Elusive
articles.summary: US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators.
articles.body: US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators. US officials told news agencies on November 17 that American forces had struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said it had launched an attack on a US military site in Bahrain. AFP quoted an unnamed US official as saying that US fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile launch site on Qeshm Island." Iranian Top Cleric Visits Bosnia As Tehran Seeks Opening To Europe The official added that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets." US officials said there were no injuries or damages in the latest Iranian strikes. The IRGC had said its forces targeted a US-operated radar system in Bahrain, where the US Navy's Fifth Fleet is based. The small island nation has been hit often by Iranian drones and missiles, fired in retaliation for US-Israeli air strikes on Iran. "Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said on November 17. Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica was quoted by AFP as labeling the flare-up of violence a "deliberate testing of boundaries rather than an immediate return to full-scale warfare." "Both Washington and Tehran are pushing the envelope, probing each other's red lines and trying to establish how far they can escalate without provoking a response that spirals beyond their control," he said. While all-out air strikes have largely subsided in the war that began at the end of February with US and Israeli air strikes on Iran, there has been no comprehensive peace deal and occasional flareups threaten to reignite the war. The US has continued to blockade Iranian ports, preventing it from exporting oil products and causing deep shortages in its economy, while travel through the crucial Strait of Hormuz remains perilous amid the threat of Iranian strikes. Meanwhile, Bahrain and Kuwait early on November 18 issued warnings to civilians to take shelter amid threats of incoming Iranian missiles and drones. Bahrain's military said it "confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today...before they could achieve their objectives." It later issued the all-clear call. "The General Command affirmed that...the Bahrain Defense Force's air defense systems intercepted a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks," the Bahrain News Agency said. Kuwait's military said it was hitting back at "hostile drone attacks" and urged residents to follow security and safety advice. "The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks," the military said on X. Iranian Security Chief Insists Enriched Uranium Won't Leave Country The attacks come as Iranian officials met with Qatari mediators on November 17 for talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," Qatari spokesman Majed Al Ansari said. At the same time, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi travel to Oman, which has also acted as a mediator, for meetings. The Omani Foreign Ministry said he discussed safeguarding ship lanes and ensuring the smooth flow of global trade. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump is scheduled to take part in a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on November 19 in Shenzhen, in southern China. The wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine are likely to be on the agenda. Trump has said he might refrain from renewing large-scale attacks on Iran if talks proceed, but he has also said he no longer feels it is necessary to reach a deal with Tehran, saying the war has already been won. articles.title: Qatar warns Gulf escalation poses 'grave danger' and announces new talks with Iran
articles.summary: Qatar warns the US and Iran to "avoid any escalation" as Iran's new attacks in Bahrain and its strikes on Gulf shipping are putting diplomacy under pressure. Qatar's foreign ministry announces new talks with Tehran, aiming to bridge the divide between US and Iran.
articles.body: Qatar warned on Tuesday that the ongoing escalation in the Gulf poses a “grave danger” to the chances of a deal between the US and Iran, as it announced a meeting with Iranian officials later in the day.Dr. Majed Al Ansari, spokesperson for Qatar’s foreign ministry, said the risks extended “not only to freedom of navigation and the global economy, but also to the chances of reaching an agreement”.Speaking at a weekly briefing in Doha, he urged all sides to exercise restraint and avoid further escalation that could undermine negotiations.The meeting with Iranian officials would focus on proposals already under discussion, he said. He did not give a location or name the participants, describing it as part of regular contacts aimed at narrowing differences between Washington and Tehran.“Today’s meeting with the Iranian side will take place as part of mediation efforts and an exchange of views on the current proposals,” the Qatari diplomat said, adding that Tuesday's meeting aims to bridge the divide between US and Iran.His comments came after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched drones at a US radar system at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa Airbase on Tuesday.Bahrain, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, and US' Central Command (CENTCOM) said that they intercepted the drones, without any damage.Separately, Iran's attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz continued on Tuesday with a tanker’s crew being unaccounted for after the ship was struck for a second time north of Oman’s Khasab, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Tuesday. The second strike caused a fire on board.US President Donald Trump has said he will maintain the naval blockade on Iran, while Tehran continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for Gulf oil and gas exports.Cost of a prolonged stand-offAl Ansari warned that the continuing stand-off was affecting global energy markets and food security, as well as the economies and security of Gulf states.“It is in no one’s interest to remain in this situation and enter a stalemate,” he said.Asked about Qatar’s contacts with its Gulf neighbours, he said coordination was continuing, pointing to recent meetings with Saudi and Emirati officials.Diplomatic efforts were also under way in Oman, where Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met his Omani counterpart, Badr Albusaidi, on Tuesday. Oman’s foreign ministry said they discussed ways to prevent further escalation and protect international shipping.

articles.title: Iran claims drone attack on US radar system at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain
articles.summary: Bahrain was heavily targeted earlier in the war, which started in February, but had been peaceful for weeks until an Iranian drone attack on Friday. A second followed on Sunday.
articles.body: Blasts echoed over the Bahraini capital Manama on Tuesday, as Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched a drone attack, the third in five days after a weeks-long lull.Bahrain's armed forces intercepted "Iranian aerial attacks in the kingdom's skies", according to state television, while Iran's Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.Bahrain's Interior Ministry, in a post on X, warned of a "possible threat" and called on the country's residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe place and follow only official sources for information on developments.Bahraini officials also said the country's air defence systems had intercepted attacks from Iran.No confirmed report has yet been released on any impact of Iranian drones on the radar system at Sheikh Isa base or on the extent of any possible damage.The public relations arm of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps described the pre-dawn attack on Tuesday as a response to what it called "the continued violation of the airspace of the Islamic Republic of Iran" by US military drones.It said the operation formed part of ongoing air-defence and electronic warfare measures to track, destroy and capture US drones of the MQ and MQM-170 series."Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.The Guards also warned that continued use of regional bases and military facilities for actions against Iran would not go unanswered.Bahrain was heavily targeted earlier in the war, which started in February, but had been peaceful for weeks until an Iranian drone attack on Friday. A second followed on Sunday.Friday's strike was the first Iranian attack against a Gulf country since early September.The US military said it had shot down two drones launched Friday by Iranian forces, while the Bahraini army said it had intercepted Sunday's attack.Bahrain, which hosts a major US naval base, has experienced numerous Iranian attacks since US-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the Middle East war in February.Since September, the conflict has mainly been restricted to the area around the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with the US blockading Iranian ports and Tehran attempting to control the oil shipping route.The Middle East war will be on the agenda during an unprecedented trilateral summit between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, scheduled this week in China, according to the White House.As talks aimed at ending the war appear to be deadlocked, a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, is operating in the Middle East, the US military said on Monday.

As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.
articles.body: Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week. For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures. Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship. US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency. The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions. For years now, advanced computer chips have been a key battleground in the US-China rivalry because they are essential for AI, supercomputing and military technology. Chinese officials are worried this scandal could strengthen voices in Washington who argue in favour of further limiting Chinese access to cutting-edge American tech. Just this week, the Trump administration introduced new export restrictions on Chinese firms that access advanced US chips in third countries such as Malaysia, Thailand or Brazil. They typically do this by renting computing power in data centres abroad to train their AI models. But some of the firms, like the one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips to China, although they have denied this. Until now, this controversy appeared to be a sideshow in US-China relations. But with Beijing calling the new rules "economic coercion" on the eve of Trump arriving in Shenzhen, there is a growing risk it could become something much bigger. Watch: Jensen Huang speaks to the BBC's Faisal Islam in 2025 Democrats, who will control Congress come January, have made their position clear. Last Wednesday top Democrat Ted Lieu told Politico the Trump administration had been "1,000%" too deferential to Nvidia, putting national security at risk, while fellow Democrat Zoe Lofgren suggested Congress would now be more likely to restrict sales of AI chips to China. Beijing's foreign ministry had described the spy claims as a "smear against China". "The US should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives to find pretexts for imposing technological blockades," spokesperson Mao Ning said last week. The ministry also seemed keen to keep the meeting on track, saying the two countries had kept "close communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state". For the last year, Trump and Xi have been seeking to stabilise relations after a damaging tariff war that almost brought trade between the two countries to a standstill. The Trump administration's decision to permit sales of advanced Nvidia H200 chips to China in late 2025 was seen as evidence that both sides were searching for areas of co-operation, even while competition intensified. It was a rare move given Washington had spent years trying to limit China's access to the most advanced chips. Many in the US have long viewed these chips as a national security issue, arguing they could strengthen China's military and surveillance capabilities. Jensen Huang, who rejects that claim , advocated lifting bans on the export of high-performing chips to China. Beijing argues the restrictions are an attempt to contain its rise. History has taught Beijing and Washington that spy scandals rarely remain confined to the intelligence world. Analysts in China already see echoes of an incident in 2023 when a suspected surveillance balloon drifted through the skies over the US before an American fighter jet shot it down. Beijing insisted it was a civilian meteorological airship that had strayed off course. The suspected Chinese spy balloon was shot down days after it was spotted over the US But a planned trip by then US Secretary of State Antony Blinken was cancelled and communication between the two governments deteriorated sharply. The incident showed how quickly a security dispute could overwhelm diplomatic efforts and push relations into a deep freeze. "The mere passage of a balloon sent American public opinion and politicians into a state of high alert, as if a "Chinese threat" were looming directly overhead," said the state media outlet, the Global Times this week as it made a direct comparison with the Nvidia scandal. "No-one on the US side has ever apologised or taken responsibility for the genuine damage this caused to US-China relations," it added. The state-run outlet also questioned why the Nvidia story had emerged so soon after "the hard-won detente" between Beijing and Washington, following a meeting between the two countries' leaders in September. "Is someone behind the scenes pushing an agenda and stirring up confrontation?" it asked. China's economy remains under pressure and is increasingly reliant on exports. Xi needs trade to keep flowing and this meeting is a key stepping stone to replacing the current trade truce that is due to expire in January. Meanwhile Trump has repeatedly touted his close relationship with Xi and argued that maintaining dialogue is essential to managing competition between the two powers. The US president is in his last two years and faces an uphill struggle to pass domestic legislation after the midterms. To counter this, he could be looking for some foreign policy wins. He may also hope for Xi's help to end the war in the Middle East. Neither side will want to be discussing intelligence concerns and technology controls instead of trade, investment and economic co-operation. The summit is also being carefully choreographed by Beijing to show off its technological prowess in Shenzhen - a deeply symbolic choice of city. It's home to some of the country's biggest tech companies and has become a showcase for Beijing's ambitions in AI and advanced manufacturing. Also, given Washington's tighter restrictions on advanced chips, Beijing has options for retaliation. One of its most powerful tools is its dominance of key rare earth minerals. China processes much of the world's supply for materials that are used in everything from electric vehicles and smartphones to military equipment. Analysts have long warned that technological restrictions can trigger a cycle of retaliation in which each side reaches for its strongest economic leverage. That would shift the current trend of US-China relations from engagement back towards mutual suspicion. articles.title: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
articles.summary: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
articles.body: A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. Counter Terrorism Policing said he is now in US custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said it had "nothing to do with it". British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. The day after Tyner's arrest on 10 November, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to. The US serviceman is understood to have been based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire On Tuesday, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. Tyner's arrest was the result of a long-running operation by MI5 - the UK's domestic intelligence and security agency - in collaboration with the FBI, the BBC understands. He had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq, but at the time of his arrest was working with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester - where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information which would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia. Detectives sent the Crown Prosecution Service a file on the senior US soldier's alleged spying for consideration - allegations described by the head of Counter Terrorism Policing as "extremely serious." But at that stage the Attorney General's Office in London got involved. As did the US authorities. And now the decision has been taken that Lieutenant Colonel Tyner should be taken into custody by the US Military. It means he will not stand trial in the UK, but under US Uniform Code of Military Justice. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added.

Serbian Court Seeks Arrest of Kosovo Serb Kingpin Radoicic
articles.summary: Court asks police to issue arrest warrant for businessman and politician after he failed to report to police – violating measures imposed as part of probe into a 2023 shootout in the Kosovo village of Banjska/Banjske.
articles.body: The Higher Court in Belgrade has ordered Milan Radoicic’s detention and that an arrest warrant be issued for him for violating a measure prohibiting him from leaving his place of residence, according to media reports on Tuesday. Radoicic failed to report to Belgrade’s Savski Venac police station on November 15, when he was required to confirm that he was still at his registered place of residence, as ordered by the court. The businessman and former vice-president of the Belgrade-backed Srpska Lista party, who is seen as a ‘kingpin’ operator among Serbs in northern Kosovo, is under investigation over an armed attack on the Kosovo village of Banjska/Banjske in September 2023. The Higher Court in Belgrade confiscated his passport in 2023, and warned that detention may be imposed if he violated the terms imposed on his freedom of movement, which included not leaving his place of residence. He was ordered to appear at a police station twice a month. Belgrade Higher Prosecutor’s Office questioned Radoicic in September 2023 about allegations that he had obtained large amounts of weapons and took them to northern Kosovo, where an armed Serb group was involved in the deadly shootout with Kosovo police in Banjska/Banjske on September 24 that year. Prosecutors allege that Radoicic “procured weapons, ammunition and explosive devices” in Bosnia, “which were delivered to him in the city of Belgrade”. They claim Radoicic “transported and stored [the weapons] in unspecified locations” in Kosovo and “hid them in abandoned buildings and forests”. In the ensuing shootout in Banjska/Banjske, a Kosovo policeman was killed. Three of the gunmen also died. In September 2023, Radoicic said he took sole responsibility for the shootout, while he described as a “defence” operation against the Kosovo authorities, without the knowledge of his political party, Srpska Lista, or the Serbian authorities in Belgrade.

articles.title: 14:42 302 people killed in various incidents in Kyrgyzstan since start of 2026
articles.summary: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration.
articles.body: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration. According to him, despite a decline in the overall number of incidents compared with last year, the death toll has increased by 24. As of November 15, 2026, material damage caused by the reported incidents amounted to 1,269 billion soms, according to the Ministry of Emergency Situations. For comparison, 3,816 incidents were recorded during the same period in 2025, claiming 278 lives. Material damage amounted to 1,735 billion soms. Thus, the number of incidents decreased by 167, while material damage fell by 466 million soms. The minister also reported that 42 emergencies had been registered in the country since the beginning of this year, claiming 42 lives. The damage amounted to 468,502 million soms. During the same period last year, 14 emergencies were recorded, leaving 32 people dead, while the damage was estimated at 60 million soms. A total of 2,709 fires have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of the year, 509 fewer than during the same period in 2025. Material damage caused by fires amounted to 1,213 billion soms, down 518 million soms from last year’s figure. Twenty-two people died in fires, compared with 46 in 2025. articles.title: Yerevan suggests car restrictions after Pashinyan’s wife says traffic can cause ‘a heart attack’
articles.summary: Amidst growing criticism over traffic congestion and overcrowded public transport in Yerevan, Mayor Tigran Avinyan has called for possible restrictions on the number of cars and promised to bring proposed measures up for public discussion later in November. The proposal came shortly after Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s wife, Anna Hakobyan, said getting around the capital could cause a ‘heart attack’.
articles.body: Amidst growing criticism over traffic congestion and overcrowded public transport in Yerevan, Mayor Tigran Avinyan has called for possible restrictions on the number of cars and promised to bring proposed measures up for public discussion later in November. The proposal came shortly after Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s wife, Anna Hakobyan, said getting around the capital could cause a ‘heart attack’. Despite major public transport reforms, including the purchase of new buses and the replacement of minibuses, the city’s transport problems remain unresolved, continuing to fuel public discontent and criticism online over long traffic jams during peak hours, overcrowded transport and bus stops, and public transport delays. Avinyan addressed the issue during a municipal administrative session on Monday, calling it a ‘multilayered’ problem and pointing to major contributing factors, including the growing number of cars and population, along with poor driving habits. In order to address the problem, Avinyan called for restrictions on the number of cars allowed to circulate in the capital, including measures targeting older and highly polluting vehicles. According to him, the number of cars in Yerevan is growing ‘exponentially’, primarily attributing this to Armenia’s economic growth and rising incomes. Over the past 12 years, the number of cars in Armenia had doubled from 500,000 to 1 million, Deputy Mayor Suren Grigoryan said, adding that around 15,000 new cars are registered in Yerevan annually. ‘The first issue we need to discuss is limiting the number of cars circulating in Yerevan. If [critics] tell us that we are once again talking about restrictions, I want to insist that we are already living under restrictions today, because the number of cars has already restricted all of us. Worst of all, it has restricted public transport’, Avinyan said. Avinyan argued that public transport was not underperforming because there were too few buses or trolleybuses, but because of the space taken up by private cars during peak hours, making it difficult for public transport to reach stops, causing even worse traffic jams. He added that public transport should operate ‘like a Swiss watch’, warning that driving in Yerevan would become less convenient in the future as dedicated lanes prioritising public transport are introduced. Avinyan went on to criticise poor driving habits and traffic violations, adding that with the increased number of cars, ‘just 50 cars can bring a city to a standstill’ due to their violations. Among other proposals, he also suggested dividing Yerevan into different zones, introducing dedicated bus lanes, and discussing measures to encourage children to attend schools closer to home. Avinyan stressed the need to create more jobs outside the capital, arguing that the concentration of employment opportunities in Yerevan is contributing to increased traffic. The municipality was instructed on Monday to develop a set of regulations and present the proposed measures for public discussion by the end of next week. The discussion followed criticism from Hakobyan, who recently complained about traffic in Yerevan in a social media video on 10 November. ‘Getting from one place to another in Yerevan is enough for a heart attack’, she said. ‘There are people for whom finding an answer to this question long ago has been part of their job. Although, apparently, it is a somewhat more difficult task than granting construction permits to companies making million-dollar investments’, Hakobyan added, in an apparent reference to the municipality. Avinyan appeared to respond to Hakobyan on Monday by denying that construction growth in the city worsened its traffic. Instead, he said that the growth of Yerevan’s population is not because of construction, but was rather due to the influx of refugees from Nagorno-Karabakh and of foreigners, mainly Russians and Russian—Armenians, due to Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine. Furthermore, Avinyan defended the continued construction, arguing that slowing the pace of real estate development would have serious consequences for Yerevan’s property and rental markets. He claimed new buildings helped moderate rental prices, which he suggested would otherwise be significantly higher, despite them already being disproportionately high with Yerevan rental pricing and prices of real estate constantly sparking debate online. He also said the municipality had a direct financial interest in construction projects launched since 2022, with fees introduced in 2023 helping fund improvements to hundreds of courtyards, football pitches, roads, and sewage systems. articles.title: Constitutional Court rejects UNM motion seeking clarification of legal standards in party ban case
articles.summary: The Plenum of Georgia’s Constitutional Court has rejected a motion filed by United National Movement (UNM) representative Zaza Bibilashvili, ruling that procedural decisions already adopted by the Court are not subject to review.
articles.body: The Plenum of Georgia’s Constitutional Court has rejected a motion filed by United National Movement (UNM) representative Zaza Bibilashvili, ruling that procedural decisions already adopted by the Court are not subject to review. The motion, submitted during ongoing hearings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban opposition political parties, called on the Court to clarify the legal standards applicable to the proceedings before issuing its final judgment. Bibilashvili requested that the Court issue an interim ruling or written clarification addressing three key issues: the specific matters requiring proof under Article 23 of the Georgian Constitution for each defendant; the allocation of the burden of proof, taking into account the presumption of constitutionality of political parties’ activities; and the standards of proof and evaluation of evidence. He argued that establishing these standards in advance was essential to ensuring that the defendants could effectively exercise their right to defense. “We are dealing with a case of such magnitude, as citizens of this country, that I do not understand how 20 or 30 minutes, or even a day, could compare with the potentially catastrophic consequences this case may have,” Bibilashvili said. He warned that the consequences could extend beyond the prohibition of political parties, suggesting that Russia could use the proceedings to justify its own actions. Bibilashvili claimed that the Court faced a choice between clarifying the applicable legal standards before the remaining procedural stages or establishing them only in its final judgment, when the parties would no longer have an opportunity to adjust their defense accordingly. Responding to the motion, Georgian Dream representative Archil Gorduladze accused Bibilashvili of using the courtroom for political statements rather than addressing legal issues. Gorduladze argued that the opposition was attempting to revisit procedural matters already considered by the Court and questioned why the defendants continued to seek clarification of the allegations against them. “Make up your minds about whether this lawsuit contains evidence. Make up your minds about whether you have answers to the numerous allegations we have presented concerning systemic crimes,” Gorduladze said. He also referred to an earlier motion by Coalition for Change representative Nika Gvaramia, who had requested advance clarification of when a potential decision banning political parties would take effect. Gorduladze argued that both motions sought to have the Court determine aspects of its eventual ruling before completing its examination of the case. Following consideration of the arguments, the Constitutional Court's Plenum rejected Bibilashvili’s motion. Announcing the decision, Judge Revaz Nadaraia explained that the motion effectively challenged procedural rulings previously issued by the Plenum in response to requests from the parties. “Rulings adopted by the Court's Plenum are not subject to review,” Nadaraia stated. He also rejected the request for advance clarification of evidentiary standards, arguing that it would effectively require the Court to indicate beforehand which evidence it intended to use and for what purpose. “This is inconceivable,” Nadaraia said. The proceedings concern a constitutional lawsuit initiated by Georgian Dream seeking the prohibition of opposition political parties. The case remains under consideration by the Constitutional Court.

articles.title: Buchukuri: ‘The issues being examined by the Constitutional Court are irrelevant’
articles.summary: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned.
articles.body: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned. To be honest, the issues the court is examining are so irrelevant that there is no constitutional basis for them. None of the questions raised by the judges yesterday concerned our party, because we have always held a different position, from vetting to our non-participation in the alliance,” Buchukuri told journalists at the Constitutional Court. She said she was interested in what questions the judges would put to her party, adding that the proceedings did not constitute a genuine legal process. “Ultimately, you know that what is currently taking place at the Constitutional Court is not a legal process. Unfortunately, the parties present here, including the respondent side, cannot influence the decision. Society can see the difference in terms of competence. People can sense it. They may not follow specific legal terms and arguments, but they naturally recognize it,” she said. The Constitutional Court is hearing a lawsuit filed by Georgian Dream seeking to ban three opposition political groups: the United National Movement, the Coalition for Change and Strong Georgia. The ruling party accuses them of violating constitutional principles and seeks to have their activities prohibited. articles.title: US addresses rumors of a Nov. 17 blackout
articles.summary: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated on X that social media reports of power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true. What is actually happening on Nov. 17?
articles.body: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated on X that social media reports of power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true. FEMA and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will jointly conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System (EAS). The test is scheduled to begin at 2:20 p.m. ET and last approximately one minute. Regular TV and radio broadcasts will be interrupted by a test message in English and Spanish. «It lasts 1 minute, and no action is required. No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio at approximately 2:20 PM ET,» the agency said in a post on X. FEMA stressed that the test is unrelated to any emergency and does not involve outages affecting electricity, communications, internet or banking services. Claims of a digital catastrophe allegedly set to strike on Nov. 17, 2026, has been widely circulating on social media. The authors of the posts claim that hackers will breach banks worldwide, wipe out bank account balances and shut down the internet for three months. Media reports say that on Oct. 31, a user going by the nickname Wesley posted about an impending collapse. He claimed that an acquaintance with ties to the darknet had warned him about it. The author provided no verifiable evidence. Initially, the post mentioned a mysterious «COVID 2.0.» Details about bank breaches, wiped-out account balances and a prolonged internet shutdown emerged as the story spread further. Furthermore, social media users began referencing an episode of «The Simpsons,» titled «It’s a Blunderful Life» (Season 35, 2023), in which a power outage hits the fictional town of Springfield on Nov. 17. However, the animated series makes no mention of either 2026 or global cyberattacks. Kursiv.media previously reported that several major U.S. banks experienced widespread disruptions to their online services on Nov. 16. In a separate report, Kursiv.media examined rumors of a «digital apocalypse» allegedly scheduled for Nov. 17. Kazakhstanis were warned of mass cyberattacks, wiped-out bank account balances and a three-month internet shutdown. However, the country’s Ministry of Emergency Situations dismissed these reports.

It reveals the mounting human and economic toll of extreme weather events,” the group said. The Climate Risk Index ranked Dominica, Myanmar, and Honduras as the hardest-hit countries over the 30-year period. Nine of the 10 worst-affected countries were middle-income economies, with the Bahamas the only high-income country in the group. In 2025 alone, 367 extreme weather events killed nearly 35,000 people, affected more than 100 million, and caused over $158 billion in direct losses. Jamaica, Sri Lanka, and Spain were the hardest hit that year. “Heatwaves were by far the deadliest extreme weather events in 2025,” Germanwatch said. They killed more than 24,000 people, accounting for nearly 70% of reported deaths. The group said heat waves are “severely underreported in regions such as sub-Saharan Africa.” Storms caused the greatest economic damage, with $64.8 billion in direct losses in 2025. They accounted for 58% of losses over the three decades covered by the index. “COP31 must deliver ambitious action on adaptation, loss and damage, and mitigation,” Germanwatch said, calling on major emitters and fossil fuel producers to increase financial support.

articles.title: Armenian, Russian Officials Open Railway Talks
articles.summary: Speaking after the meeting held in Yerevan on Tuesday, Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Davit Ivanian described the discussions as constructive and practical, noting that the two sides focused on specific railway directions and sections. “The talks took place in a very friendly, fairly normal, down-to-earth and businesslike atmosphere regarding concrete directions and sections,” Ivanian said.
articles.body: Speaking after the meeting held in Yerevan on Tuesday, Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Davit Ivanian described the discussions as constructive and practical, noting that the two sides focused on specific railway directions and sections. “The talks took place in a very friendly, fairly normal, down-to-earth and businesslike atmosphere regarding concrete directions and sections,” Ivanian said. When asked whether the Russian side had substantiated the efficiency of its management of the railway system, Ivanian said the discussions had not yet reached that stage. “We have not yet come to that stage to be able to answer that question,” he said. The joint Armenian-Russian working group was established in October for a three-month term to address issues related to the operation of Armenia’s railways, which have been managed since 2008 by South Caucasus Railway, a wholly owned subsidiary of the state-run Russian Railways company. According to Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinian, the group is mandated to submit proposals aimed at increasing the competitiveness of the Armenian railway network. Ivanian, who leads the Armenian delegation, said further steps will be determined based on the conclusions reached at the end of the three-month discussion format. The Russian side in the working group is represented by Deputy Transport Minister Aleksei Shilo and Russian Railways Deputy CEO Vyacheslav Pavlovsky. According to Ivanian, during the opening session, the sides also addressed proposals to restore two currently non-operational cross-border railway sections: one running from the Armenian village of Yeraskh to the border with Azerbaijan’s Nakhichevan exclave, and another from the Armenian town of Gyumri to the Turkish border. Ivanian noted that because it was the group’s first meeting, many technical details remain to be addressed in future sessions. “But it was a very normal, to-the-point discussion,” he added. In early October, Moscow stated that it was awaiting Yerevan’s response to a Russian proposal regarding the restoration of those two border sections. The establishment of the working group followed months of friction over the future of the concession. Earlier this year, Yerevan proposed that Moscow transfer the management of Armenia’s railway network to a third country acceptable to both Armenia and Russia. Moscow rejected the proposal, warning that any unilateral alteration of the concession terms or termination of the contract could prompt Russia to demand the return of roughly $400 million in investments made in the network. Tensions eased in October when Russian Railways CEO Oleg Belozyorov visited Yerevan and met with Pashinian. Following those talks, both sides announced their intention to continue joint work. Under the 30-year concession agreement signed in 2008, Russian Railways is entitled to manage Armenia’s rail infrastructure through its local subsidiary until 2038. To trigger an optional 10-year extension of the deal, the two sides must submit formal proposals to each other by August 2027.

articles.summary: The UN court has denied wartime Bosnian Serb Army officer Dragomir Milosevic’s early release request for a fourth time, citing a lack of ‘sufficient signs’ of rehabilitation.
articles.body: This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp Dragomir Milosevic in court in The Hague, December 2004 . Photo: EPA/JUAN VRIJDAG. The UN’s International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals in The Hague announced on Tuesday that it has rejected a request for the early release of Dragomir Milosevic, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Bosnian Serb Army, who was sentenced to 29 years in prison for crimes against civilians in besieged Sarajevo. The president of the International Residual Mechanism, Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, stated in her decision that although Milosevic meets the eligibility requirements for consideration for early release, she believes that the request should be denied. “The high gravity of his crimes strongly militates against granting him early release and Milosevic has not demonstrated sufficient signs of rehabilitation. Further, there is no evidence before me that establishes the existence of compelling humanitarian grounds which would warrant overriding this negative assessment,” Gatti Santana explained. The decision states that Milosevic, who is now 84, clearly suffers from several chronic health conditions. It also states that his behaviour in prison has been consistently good. “However, I have no information that would suggest that Milosevic has engaged in any further reflection about his crimes and specific role in them, or any other positive conduct that could demonstrate a level of rehabilitation that would warrant the exceptional relief of early release,” Gatti Santana said. Milosevic was convicted of bearing responsibility for terrorising civilians in besieged Sarajevo with a campaign of sniper and artillery attacks as commander of the Bosnian Serb Army’s Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. The Hague Tribunal also convicted the wartime Bosnian Serb political and military leaders, Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic, and another former commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, Stanislav Galic, of similar offences. During the 44-month siege of Sarajevo by Bosnian Serb forces, more than 11,000 residents of Sarajevo were killed, including around 1,600 children.

articles.title: Kazakh lawmakers turn to AI to draft new child safety legislation
articles.summary: Members of Kazakhstan’s Kurultai, recently inaugurated unicameral parliament, have drafted a bill aimed at protecting children online with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed legislation introduces restrictions on online games and purchases made by children on e-commerce platforms, according to Dinara Zakiyeva, deputy speaker of the Kurultai.
articles.body: Members of Kazakhstan’s Kurultai , recently inaugurated unicameral parliament, have drafted a bill aimed at protecting children online with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed legislation introduces restrictions on online games and purchases made by children on e-commerce platforms, according to Dinara Zakiyeva , deputy speaker of the Kurultai. Zakiyeva said the draft law, titled «On the Digital and Information Safety of Children,» was the first piece of legislation in Kazakhstan to be drafted using the AI-Quryltai intelligent platform, which incorporates an AI model. She added that the system is capable of performing legal reasoning. «All proposals generated by AI-Quryltai during the drafting process were reviewed and further refined by the MPs involved in developing the bill,» Zakiyeva said. The proposed legislation establishes requirements for labeling and describing online games. Game descriptions must include information about potential digital risks, such as in-game purchases and features that allow users to communicate or exchange messages. The bill also proposes mandatory screening of online services intended for children by an authorized government body. Officials will assess digital products for compliance with established requirements. If violations are identified, the authorities will be empowered to restrict access to, remove or block the applications and games in question . «A similar approach is proposed for regulating interactions between minors and electronic commerce platforms, particularly when it comes to purchasing goods through online marketplaces,» Zakiyeva said. Furthermore, the bill would require all digital platforms to implement parental controls. This means children would not be able to view or download digital content, applications or games that have not been properly labeled and verified.

articles.title: HOWO and Volvo trucks to be manufactured in Kazakhstan, talks with Mercedes underway
articles.summary: Construction of the Saran Machinery plant in Saran, Karaganda region, which will manufacture Chinese HOWO and Sinotruk trucks, is nearing completion. Meanwhile, Volvo trucks are set to be manufactured in Almaty, with negotiations underway over the potential manufacturing of Mercedes-Benz trucks.
articles.body: Construction of the Saran Machinery plant in Saran, Karaganda region, which will manufacture Chinese HOWO and Sinotruk trucks, is nearing completion. Meanwhile, Volvo trucks are set to be manufactured in Almaty, with negotiations underway over the potential manufacturing of Mercedes-Benz trucks. During a government meeting, Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov said the country would localize production of heavy-duty trucks made by international brands to develop its logistics potential and modernize its vehicle fleet. «Manufacturing of HOWO, Sinotruk and Scania trucks has already been established. Work is underway to increase the local content of their components. In addition, manufacturing of Volvo trucks is planned to begin in Almaty by the end of this year, while negotiations with Mercedes are ongoing,» Bektenov said. Notably, Volvo FH13 trucks will be manufactured in Kazakhstan at the Astana Motors plant. The agreement was signed in June. Industry and Construction Minister Yersaiyn Nagaspayev presented the Saran Machinery plant project as one of the key industrial projects scheduled for implementation in 2026. The facility is expected to manufacture up to 10,000 HOWO trucks annually. The project is valued at 24 billion tenge (approximately $53.9 million). At the initial stage, only truck cabs and chassis will be manufactured, with welding and painting lines scheduled to become operational later in 2026. In the longer term, the plant is expected to transition to full-cycle production using domestically produced components. The project is being implemented jointly with Chinese truck manufacturer Sinotruk. The Kazakhstani partner is MashZavod (Saran Machine-Building Plant), controlled by Timur Karbayev . Nagaspayev also named several other key industrial investment projects planned for 2026. One of them is the VOLTREX motor oil plant, currently under construction in Shymkent, with an estimated project cost of 48 billion tenge (approximately $107.9 million). The facility is designed to manufacture 50,000 units annually. The company’s founder is Yerkebulan Ilyassov , son of Saidulla Kozhabayev , the majority shareholder and founder of Alageum Group. Kozhabayev ranks 47th on Forbes’ list of Kazakhstan’s richest people, with an estimated net worth of $215 million. The third project involves the manufacture of pipes and pipe fittings by QazExpo Centre-Pipe, with an estimated investment of 26.8 billion tenge ($60.2 million). The facility is designed to produce 20,000 units annually. The company already operates a pipe manufacturing facility in Uralsk. It is owned by Lazat Yessekeyeva and Sergey Martsev .

Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact
articles.summary: Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join next round of demonstrations as US president arrives for Asean summit Asean and Apec summits – as it happened Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit.
articles.body: Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit. Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site. Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people in widespread protests held in the days leading up to the summit, with large parts of the capital closed off and tight security in place. Some burned effigies of Trump and faced off with police officers armed with batons and shields. Slogans on placards called the American leader the world’s “No 1 terrorist” in protests held on Monday. Demonstrators angry at the cost of living and energy shock caused by the Iran war, and the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals, tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center on Monday, but were blocked by police. Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community. Large sections of central Manila were closed to the public as part of the security cordon and public holidays put in place for the Asean summit. After departing from Fairbanks in Alaska, Trump emerged from Air Force One at Ninoy Aquino International airport at 5.54pm local time (0954 GMT), live video showed. Trump will meet with the leaders of Australia, Japan and India on Tuesday night before heading to Shenzhen in China on Wednesday. There he will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit and hold trilateral talks with China’s president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia. The backlash against Trump follows the ousting of the boss of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, and allegations members of the US administration, including the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, knew about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Protest leader Renato Reyes blamed the arrests in Manila on the heavy handed response of the government on the president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, calling Monday the largest single day of police arrests since Marcos came to office in 2022. “It is really crazy that the Philippine government is rolling out the red carpet for someone who has been so flatly rejected by the American people,” Reyes said. “Trump started a war that devastated the global economy and pushed oil prices in the Philippines to historic highs. It has caused untold suffering on the Filipino people. “So, yes, Trump will have to pay for his crimes and he will have to be answerable, not just to the American people, but to the people of the world.” The Philippine national police said some officers were injured during confrontations with demonstrators opposed to the summit, including when objects were allegedly thrown at officers. Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 100km from Manila. Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 26 participating signatory governments. Amnesty International said demonstrations should not be forcibly or violently dispersed. “Reports of arrests during the protests demand immediate scrutiny,” Amnesty’s director for the Philippines, Ritz Lee Santos III, said. “Authorities must explain the specific grounds for each arrest and any continued detention. Anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights must be released immediately.”

articles.title: Europe ready to talk about peace only ignoring Russia's interests — Foreign Ministry
articles.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova recalled that when it came to a possible appointment of former Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder as a European negotiator, Berlin categorically opposed it
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 17. /TASS/. The statements of German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul fit into the logic of Europe, which is ready to talk about peace only if Russia’s interests are disregarded, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said. The diplomat drew attention to Wadephul’s declaration of readiness to begin substantive negotiations with Russia on peace. According to him, Russia must realize that in this conflict "it is impossible to win on the battlefield" and a negotiated solution must be found as soon as possible. "Wadephul's statements repeat the same logic: Europe is ready to talk about peace only if Russia's interests are put aside in advance. But it won't be like that. These are not negotiations, but an ultimatum wrapped in diplomatic rhetoric, and these are dead-end reflections," Zakharova said on Telegram. She quoted Vladimir Zelensky as saying that it was Berlin that became Kiev's main defense partner. "€55 billion is for military aid alone. That is how much, according to Johann Wadephul, Germany has allocated to Ukraine since 2022 to remain Kiev's 'largest sponsor.' Not for humanitarian programs and not for reconstruction, but for the weapons that are being fired at Russian cities and civilians," the representative of the Russian diplomatic mission said. Zakharova said that money and military equipment are used for very specific tasks, namely, the targeted destruction of the Russian civilian population. As Zakharova noted, Wadephul had previously wondered whether the trilateral talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi were an ostentatious event. "And now - Wadephul's signature diplomacy. In November 2026, on the eve of the Abu Dhabi talks, Wadephul put the question bluntly: does Russia have a genuine desire to negotiate, or is this just an 'ostentatious event' designed to distract attention from military operations," she continued. "A convenient design: if Moscow is talking about peace, it means it is an 'ostentatious event,' if it is silent, it means it does not want to. Meanwhile, it was Germany that refused to negotiate, calling their possibility ‘a concession to Moscow’ and ‘the wrong signal for European security’," she said. She noted that when it came to a possible appointment of former Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder as a European negotiator, Berlin categorically opposed it. "As a result, Europe was again left without a channel of direct dialogue, but with fantasies about some kind of format in which Moscow would be prepared for the role of a party tacitly accepting European conditions," the representative of the Russian diplomatic mission summed up.
